v36_quote: 13,512 peptide–acquisition–seed observations through the mass route
v42_quote: De novo predictions carry residual order ambiguity that AlphaNovo records as bags, and near-isobaric composition ambiguity that a swap table can enumerate. We tested whether admitting either at the lookup step improved the final identification list. Over 717 acquisitions (15 CAMPI, 50 healthy stool, 306 PREDICT and 346 CapScan; nine acquisitions without a reproducible exact baseline were excluded), admitting recorded bags added 67,875 peptide–acquisition events and removed 48,358 (net +19,517, positive in 483 of 717). Restricting the bag route to predictions with at most 8, 4 or 2 orderings gave net changes of +14,368, +9,210 and −216 (positive in 476, 455 and 405 acquisitions). Admitting mass-equivalent substitutions from the full swap table added 430,798 and removed 568,964 events (net −138,166, positive in 53 of 717). Across all 726 acquisitions and two seeds, shuffled-query controls yielded 170,441 peptide–acquisition–seed observations through the mass route, and the exact and bag routes accepted peptides in a single acquisition–seed, where a shuffled query selected abundant human titin (Supplementary Table 5). The separate matched comparison and fragment-ion check are detailed below and in Supplementary Fig. 2e,f.
